faq.a: Aissatou is associated with the Arabic form عَائِشَة, whose core sense is aissatou; aisha (west african form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Aissatou?
faq.a: Aissatou is associated with Arabic. Aissatou is the West African (Fulani) form of Arabic عَائِشَة (ʿĀʾisha), associated with the sense 'living, prosperous'.
Yes — the underlying form عَائِشَة is Arabic.
Aissatou can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Aissatou should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿĀʾisha is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Aissatou mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Aissatou is rendered عائشہ and carries the sense عائشہ، زندہ.

faq.q: What does Aissatou mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Aissatou is rendered عایشه and carries the sense عایشه، زنده.
A romanized syllable approximation is ais-sa-tou. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Aissatou?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Aissatou, aissatou. Script forms are عائشہ, عايشه, عایشه, عَائِشَة, आइसातु.

faq.q: Is Aissatou a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
